db-01-c1.quote: In his 1970 paper “A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks,” Codd envisioned a software architecture that would enable users to access information without expertise in, or even knowledge of, the database’s physical blueprint.
db-01-c1.claim: In 1970, IBM researcher Edgar F. Codd published a paper titled A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks.

db-01-c2.quote: A foreign key constraint specifies that the values in a column (or a group of columns) must match the values appearing in some row of another table. We say this maintains the referential integrity between two related tables.
db-01-c2.claim: A foreign key is a column whose values must match the primary key of another table.

db-02-c2.quote: The three available join strategies are: nested loop join: The right relation is scanned once for every row found in the left relation.
db-02-c2.claim: The database engine has multiple join algorithms (nested loop, hash join, merge join) and the planner picks one based on table sizes, indexes, and statistics.

db-02-c3.quote: The fundamental difference between WHERE and HAVING is this: WHERE selects input rows before groups and aggregates are computed (thus, it controls which rows go into the aggregate computation), whereas HAVING selects group rows after groups and aggregates are computed.
db-02-c3.claim: Watch out: WHERE filters rows before aggregation; HAVING filters groups after.

db-03-c1.quote: Durability The assurance that once a transaction has been committed, the changes remain even after a system failure or crash. This is one of the ACID properties.
db-03-c1.claim: Durability: once committed, the change survives crashes.

db-03-c2.quote: Read Committed is the default isolation level in PostgreSQL.
db-03-c2.claim: The default in PostgreSQL and Oracle is READ COMMITTED.

db-03-c2.text: 17.7.2.1 Transaction Isolation Levels. MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual.
db-03-c2.quote: The default isolation level for InnoDB is REPEATABLE READ.
db-03-c2.claim: The default in MySQL InnoDB is REPEATABLE READ.

db-04-c2.quote: Hash indexes store a 32-bit hash code derived from the value of the indexed column. Hence, such indexes can only handle simple equality comparisons.
db-04-c2.claim: Hash indexes are faster for exact-match lookups but useless for range queries ("all users with age between 25 and 35").

db-04-c3.quote: You can use the EXPLAIN command to see what query plan the planner creates for any query.
db-04-c3.claim: Almost every database exposes this with an EXPLAIN command.

db-05-c3.quote: CRDTs ensure that, no matter what data modifications are made on different replicas, the data can always be merged into a consistent state.
db-05-c3.claim: CRDTs (Conflict-free Replicated Data Types) are data structures whose merge operation is mathematically guaranteed to converge regardless of order.
